stories.name: Splash screen while the daemon connects, then sign-in (email + Sign in with Apple + Google, seeded accounts) landing on the dashboard; sign-up, sign-out and session-expired states seeded
'Needs you' strip listing pending gates and failed runs across all projects
Project cards grid: name, targets, stage, last activity, thumbnail
Pair-a-device entry point on the dashboard opens the safely generated QR pairing modal (short-lived, single-use)
Analytics trio: runs/week, stage durations, gate latency
Project creation is a GenUI wizard generated inline in the chat thread (name + platform targets: iOS/Android/macOS/web)
Repo connect (GitHub default, other hosts) deferred to first gate approval; also available in settings
Auto-save of every chat action with a saved/saving indicator
Header panel shows project name + current stage chip, with click-through to the dashboard/project switcher
One-scan QR pairing: single-use short-lived tailnet pre-auth key + host/nonce/key fingerprint; relayed QR fails the pin
Device list with last-seen + revoke; revoke drops the session immediately
No third-party cloud relay — self-hosted tailnet only; an agent can never mint an approval
Phone/tablet auth view is the pairing flow (scan QR or enter code) — no sign-in forms on touch devices; account sign-in lives on desktop
Push when a gate goes red (deduped per transition), deep-link into the gate card
Actionable notification: approve/reject without opening the app
Self-host tailnet (compose file) or hosted Tailscale from day one; daemon and apps are tailnet nodes in-process; approvals bind to WireGuard node identity
Private mesh CA gives trusted HTTPS origins over the mesh (arxa ADR-0036 pattern)
Intake is a chat-native interview: depth choice (simple / normal / advanced — three separate question banks per audience) is the first chat message with 3 buttons
Each question is a horizontal-carousel card inline in the conversation: free text + single/multi-choice chips + suggested answers; skippable with a visible skipped state; swipe back to revisit
All-at-once generation when the questionnaire completes: brief + story map appear as main panel artifacts; the moodboard follows as a suggested next step

Layout template picking is an intake step: app category first (closed list), then one of six archetype galleries (feed, list-detail, supporting-pane, dashboard, hero-scroll, detail-column) shown as plain colored boxes of named containers at full size in the main panel — recorded in the brief, consumed by the designer without rewriting
Evan turns a client brief into an Epic-Feature-Story map in one sitting
Surface count + kit-coverage estimate within an hour of signing, to quote honestly
A non-technical client can read and correct the story map (HTML)
Stories carry EARS-style acceptance criteria gates can check
Stage gating: the Design shell stays locked until the story map is approved (human-gate pattern); locked shells explain why and the chat nudges
Post-approval edits produce a new story-map version requiring re-approval; downstream stages get a 'map changed' badge
Live story map artifact: epics as horizontally scrolling columns, release swimlanes, story cards with live status dots (pending/in-progress/done/blocked) fed by pipeline state
Progress rollups per epic and per release on the live story map
Tapping a story opens a detail card center-stage
brief.md surface table feeds the designer; every registry surface traces to a story
Registry seeded from the brief without rewriting
Given the story map, the moodboard orchestrator fans out per-epic reference-gathering prompts and curates real apps to steal from
Each reference's key screens are captured (appbox lens) and saved with semantic filenames (ref__screen.png)
The moodboard assembles as a browsable doc linking references and shots to the epics they inform; every embedded shot verified on disk
The design stage receives the moodboard alongside the brief and consults it before authoring
Brief to clickable htmx prototype in under 10 minutes, carrying structure not pixels
Every surface designed at 390/744/1280 from targets alone (literal parity)
Target selection labels buildability on this machine (requires macOS)
The daemon drafts all screens from the approved story map in one pass; refining happens exclusively in the centered chat
Component-library components are Auto Layout by default (flow, gap, padding, alignment; child hug/fill/fixed emitted as flexbox data-attributes); off by default at artboard level, per-frame opt-out

Pin multiple screens as chat context (removable chips); in-context screens render side-by-side (rungs layout) at real device sizes with a colored outline + 'in context' tag; non-context screens stay off-canvas
Each pinned screen is a removable context chip carrying its surfaceId's spec, never the whole app
Tool-gating scopes to the in-context set: only the pinned screens' tools exposed (edit-layout, restyle, adjust-states, regenerate)
Text/token tweaks apply instantly, no model round-trip
Each message checkpoints the in-context screens only; one-tap revert, rendered before/after
Stale-selection guard: prototype changed since the in-context screens were pinned triggers re-sync or warn
Shared token/nav edit offers 'affects N screens, apply to all?' (nobody ships this)
The floating vertical filmstrip inside the design artifact is the context picker: clicking toggles a screen's in-context state
Design elements carry inspect metadata (data-inspect-role/-style/-motion/-fn): role, style, motion and function facts read straight from the markup by the inspect pass
Hash-locked freeze; approval bound to the design hash; post-approval change goes stale loudly
Drift report + brief-to-surface-to-code traceability
Freeze approval of the frozen manifest is the human gate that unlocks the Build stage
Designer declares kit usage per surface (the registry `kits` field); the declaration is validated against the kit registry and flows through structure.json to the scaffold
Chat is the centerpiece in every stage, living in the composer panel — permanent, single-state, always on the right; the retired two-state chat (centered, sliding into a floating rail) is gone
Single input path: no text inputs outside the chat — gate notes are chat replies carrying a context chip
Activity panel (left): navigation and inventory — files, surfaces, runs / artifacts / commits views
Main panel: the single render destination, an automatic multi-mode viewer — render:code/doc/image/svg/pdf/video for files, art/map/board for stage content
Main panel mode selection is fully automatic: the active shell plus the content type select the mode and panel composition — no user toggles, no tabs, no panel picking
Composer panel (right): permanent and single-state in every shell
Panel bar: on compact and medium rungs a segmented switcher picks the one visible content panel (activity / main / composer); the tabbar (compact) and railbar (medium) switch shells

Adaptive chrome defaults: expanded = header panel + activity/main/composer panels + footer panel; compact = header panel + tabbar + panel bar; medium = header panel + railbar + panel bar — overridable per project in the design brief
Panels resize via a hover handle on the inner edge only, min = current width, max = 1.5×

Footer panel: read-only stage timeline with proper labels (not clickable; animation kept), project + run state, daemon status + pending-gate dots; in the design shell it also shows the design sub-steps (artboards → inspect · fine-tune → approval → freeze); the old top stage strip is removed
Start a build, walk away; stops on red, ESC_LIMIT=3
Per-surface evidence report (screen to tests to code), not one giant diff
SARIF findings pinned to file/line with reproduce command

The run thread is the build shell's chat: stage, evidence, chart and gate cards stream in as chat messages; evidence and charts open in the main panel (the composer panel stays put — see Chat-Centric Layout)
Three gates an agent can reach but never pass; approval = human + any authenticated shell, provenance-bound (shell, device/node identity, confirm method, timestamp, hash)
Approve/reject from phone push with biometric confirm
Pre-submission checklist gate (crashes/permissions, where generated apps die)
Gate approve/reject buttons live inline on gate chat cards; a reject note is a chat reply with a gate-context chip
Build acceptance approval unlocks the deploy stage
appbox lens design-vs-built gates: pixel (SSIM), skeleton, colour (deltaE) against the frozen golden
Smoke per target: app boots, first screen renders, no crash
The pipeline auto-commits at each gate/stage with shell-scoped conventional messages (e.g. chore(intake): ...)
Commits view in the activity panel: git history with per-commit diff and CI status dots
Open-in-editor button (VS Code default, configurable editor) launches the project externally
appbox scaffolds each project's git setup: repo init, .gitignore, host connect
Files view in the activity panel: read-only generated-project tree with per-file status badges (new/changed/frozen); clicking a file opens its content in the main panel
appbox auto-captures screenshots of design + built app per surface (appbox lens)
Flows on a canvas: living captures, connections truth-derived from real navigation
Replayable named flows for gate reviews; zoom-semantic canvas keyed to story-map sections
Per-platform builds from one codebase; unbuildable targets hard-block as a named precondition, never a red gate
Payment gate at first deploy: licence required to ship; everything before it free
Export-always: ordinary Stacked MVVM in my own repo, no export tier
Guided store submission (most-cited unmet gap in every builder)
Showcase app launches on install, automatically; quality visible in minute one
First project to working prototype in 20 minutes or less, no docs (timed; over 20 is a finding)
Stubs labelled before you build against them; kit availability honest
Credential tier stated on screen (stored in the macOS Keychain)
Empty states carry wording, not blank surfaces
Multi-project management; registry CRUD; add/delete feature yields byte-identical round-trip
BYO key in OS vault, never logged; no inference metering, cost is yours and visible
Flat licence, never per-seat; pay at first deploy
Kit vendoring from targets + capabilities; dependencyMode config from day one
Appearance prefs per device: warm light/dark theme + brand accent picker (cyan/violet/blue/ember from the logo)
Language level plain/balanced/technical — every user-facing string written three ways; visual metrics render as X/100 match scores (ΔE 2.0 = 95/100 pass bar), technical level keeps raw values

One credentials surface manages every credential the generated app needs — payments, auth, maps, deploy and AI providers grouped in sections; each row shows the key name, a secret/publishable badge, a password-style input, a where-to-get link and a set/not-set chip
User adds a Stripe test key for their design app from the credentials surface; the value goes to the OS vault via the daemon, never logged, and test keys work on simulators
User sees which required keys are missing before build — the credentials surface and `appbox credentials check` report missing required keys per module
Design surfaces the required credentials by key name from the catalog for the kits a surface declares — a maps screen lists its maps keys before build

One config surface unifies the app's knobs — build targets and default locale (the appbox.config.json mirror), a credentials summary per module with missing-required badges, and shell prefs (theme, accent, jargon) — so the user reviews everything a generated app ships with in one place
A visitor gets appbox in 30 seconds: gated pipeline, own-your-code export, pay-at-deploy
The three human gates are the headline, shown not told (recorded gate flow)
Pricing page: flat licence, never per-seat, BYO key, pay at first deploy (the anti-credit-rage page)
Docs portal publishes the knowledge base (architecture, plans, research, skills) with search
Getting-started mirrors Michelle's 20 minutes: install, showcase, first prototype
Public honesty page: what is wired, what throws, what is roadmap
Recorded walkthroughs and design-vs-built comparisons (appbox lens captures) prove quality before install
Demo videos per persona journey (Evan's modes, Michelle's 20 minutes)
Download per platform: macOS dmg, daemon CLI for Windows/Linux, mobile apps, with the honest build matrix
Licence purchase and activation, pay-at-deploy explained before checkout
Changelog and release notes per version
